g.data-string: Game board and initial state • All shapes in INITIAL are copied from BOARD, so we can use BOARD examples to detect what shape is what. • Initial state defines the positions of pieces. Ideally, we would obtain a two - dimensional 8x8 array with “Regular 1” or “Regular 2” or null in each of the positions. • The red/green boxes mark some of the board positions. Ideally, we would also get an array of coordinates included in those regions. • BOARD defines types of pieces – Regular appear on the INITIAL board and King appear in the MOVES. I also added Any as a special placeholder, to be used in MOVES definitions when we want to say that jumping can be over either King or Regular piece. (The logic of that would be handled outside of the SVG.)

g.data-string: Definitions of possible moves • We will need some processing outside of the SVG notation, for example to know that there can be multiple jumps in a single round, but only one regular move in each round (and also that jumps must be preferred if both regular and jump are available), but SVG notation can define possible moves and group them into categories. • Ideally, each “MOVES” box would be parsed as array of before/after pairs where each step of the move is represented as either 2D array or as some kind of coordinate. For example, for the first move, we could get: [ (0,0,null); (1,1,”Regular 1”) ] => [ (0,0,”Regular 1”); (1,1,null) ] • Some of the arrows that define moves are labelled – this identifies the move and it is used in the bonus feature discussed below (to specify valid sequences of moves in a single round) • Alternatively, we could draw the moves with arrows pointing from the piece to possible target locations. But this is harder, because it does not specify what other pieces must/must not be on the board (when one diagram represents multiple possible moves). I think we do not want that.

g.data-string: Pieces turning into kings • When a regular piece is in a special area defined in INITIAL board state, it becomes a different kind of piece as defined in TRANSFORMS.

it becomes a different kind of piece

g.data-string: Definitions of possible combinations of moves [OPTIONAL] • Depending on the variation of the game, different moves can happen in a single round. It can be single REGULAR move, a sequence of any number REGULAR_JUMP moves, sequence of any number of single particular KING moves (they can go arbitrary distance but not change direction). We can label the arrows to distinguish what exactly moves are legal. • For example, in some variants, kings can land only immediately after piece they jump over. This means that the valid sequence is – using a regex - like notation: ((KING[RU]* KING_JUMP[RU]) | (KING[RD]* KING_JUMP[RD]) | …)* • In other variants, king can land at any later piece, i.e.: ((KING[RU]* KING_JUMP[RU] KING[RU]*) | … )* • We can define this using a state machine that defines the possible moves as in COMBINATIONS (this is bonus, but I suspect this will already work : - ))
